body: The `trackBy` binding does not account for changes and is captured during creation mode, before the input has been assigned. The problem you're having can be avoided using a method that delegates to the input.
Discussed this in the team and decided that we are not going to support it given that the case is not very common and a work-around exists. But we should detect this case and raise an error.

> The `trackBy` binding does not account for changes and is captured during creation mode, before the input has been assigned. The problem you're having can be avoided using a method that delegates to the input.

Can you elaborate on what you mean by this, maybe give an example? I'm currently facing the same problem. I have a component that has a `@for` loop in its template and a `TrackByFunction<T>` called `trackBy` as an input. Inside the component code I have the following code:

```ts
@Input()
public trackBy?: TrackByFunction<T>;

protected trackItem(index: number, item: T): unknown {
    return this.trackBy?.(index, item) ?? index;
}
```

and in the template I call it like this:

```html
@for (item of items; track trackItem(row, item); let lastItem = $last; let row = $index) {
    ...
}
```

But when I want to use the component, I just get the following error, indicating that `this` is `undefined`:

```
ERROR TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'trackBy')
    at trackItem (grid-table.component.ts:37:15)
    at createOrAttach (core.mjs:19662:73)
    at reconcile (core.mjs:19590:13)
    at Module.ɵɵrepeater (core.mjs:20517:9)
    at GridTableComponent_Template (grid-table.component.html:14:1)
    at executeTemplate (core.mjs:12159:9)
    at refreshView (core.mjs:13392:13)
    at detectChangesInView (core.mjs:13617:9)
    at detectChangesInViewIfAttached (core.mjs:13580:5)
    at detectChangesInComponent (core.mjs:13569:5)
```

issue.body:
This commits assert that the repeater instruction gets a reference to a tracking function. This change will allow us to better track occurences of https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/53628 - in certain situations a reference to a tracking function might be undefiened.

We are not fixing the underlying issue here, just getting better visibility.

issue.body:
Previously we assumed that if a `for` loop tracking function is in the form of `someMethod($index, $item)`, it will be pure so we didn't pass the parameter to bind the context to it. This appears to be risky, because we don't know if the method is trying to access `this`.

These changes play it safe by always binding method-based tracking functions.

Fixes #53628.
